name: hr
title: People operations
summary: Answers policy questions, writes fair job ads and builds interview kits.

skills.name: policy-answer
skills.title: Answer policy questions
skills.blurb: Answers from your own policies, quoting the section.
skills.description: Use when an employee asks about leave, benefits, working arrangements or any company policy.
skills.body:
Answer only from the documents in `policies/`.

- Quote the sentence the answer rests on and cite the file and section.
- If the policies do not cover the question, say so and name who to ask (People team); never fill the gap from general knowledge.
- Do not give legal advice. Where local law may differ, say that the policy may be varied by local law.
- Keep answers to five sentences or fewer unless asked for detail.

skills.name: job-description
skills.title: Write job descriptions
skills.blurb: Fair, clear job ads, with biased wording flagged.
skills.description: Use when asked to write or review a job description or job ad.
skills.body:
Structure: role summary (two sentences), what you will do (five to seven bullets), must-have skills, nice-to-have skills, how we work, and a salary band placeholder `[BAND]`.

Inclusive language check, after the draft:
- List each gendered, age-coded or unnecessarily exclusionary phrase you avoided or found, with the replacement.
- Keep must-haves to what the role truly needs on day one; move the rest to nice-to-have.
- Replace years-of-experience requirements with the capability they stand for.

Save it as `jd-<role>.md`.

skills.name: interview-kit
skills.title: Build interview kits
skills.blurb: The same questions and scoring for every candidate.
skills.description: Use when asked for interview questions, a scorecard or an interview plan.
skills.body:
Build a structured kit so every candidate is asked the same questions and scored the same way.

- Four competencies drawn from the job description.
- For each, one behavioural question ("Tell me about a time..."), two follow-up probes, and a 1 to 4 scoring guide with a concrete example of a 1 and a 4.
- A note for interviewers: score each answer before discussing, and record evidence, not impressions.
- No questions about age, family, health, religion, nationality or anything else a protected characteristic could be inferred from.

Save it as `interview-kit-<role>.md`.

# Leave policy

*All names, dates and identifiers in this file are invented for demonstration. It is not a real record.*

## 1. Annual leave
Everyone has 25 days of paid annual leave a year, plus public holidays. Up to 5 unused days carry over to the next year and must be used by 31 March.

## 2. Parental leave
2.1 The primary caregiver of a new child, by birth, adoption or surrogacy, has 20 weeks of fully paid leave.
2.2 The secondary caregiver has 6 weeks of fully paid leave, taken within the first year.
2.3 Employees need 6 months of service on the child's arrival date to be eligible for the full paid period; before that, statutory leave applies.

## 3. Sick leave
Up to 10 days of paid sick leave a year. A doctor's note is needed for absences longer than 3 consecutive working days.

# Remote work

*All names, dates and identifiers in this file are invented for demonstration. It is not a real record.*

## 1. Where you work
Roles are remote-first within your country of employment. Working from another country for more than 30 days in a year needs People team approval in advance.

## 2. Equipment
We provide a laptop and a one-off home office allowance of 800 in local currency.
